contents.html_ja: セキュアデータネットワークシステム（SDNS）アーキテクチャと、それに関連する一連の仕様は、国家安全保障局（NSA）が後援する複数組織によるプロジェクトを通じて開発されました。これらは、開放型システム間相互接続（OSI）アーキテクチャにおけるセキュリティサービスの標準化の基礎として、ここに示されています。国立標準技術研究所（NIST）は、その結果として生まれる標準の広範な採用と、これらのセキュリティサービスを幅広いベンダー製品に実装することを奨励するつもりです。
contents.html: The Secure Data Network System (SDNS) architecture and a set of associated specifications were developed through a multi-organizational project sponsored by the National Security Agency (NSA). They are presented here as a basis for standardization of security services in the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) architecture. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) intends to encourage widespread adoption of the resulting standards and the implementation of these security services into a wide spectrum of vendor products.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p7 を画像で確認し、OCR の文字を語ごとに照合した。ページの本文を 8 ブロックに組み直す。 NIST の Foreword。「(NSA). They」の句読点の脱落と、行頭記号の箇条の分断を画像どおりに直す。

contents.html_ja: NIST は、SDNS プロジェクトの第 I 期で生まれた仕様を、セキュリティ製品の政府および民間の潜在的な利用者からの検討と意見を求めるために公表します。これらの仕様は、それ自体の内部でも、国内標準および国際標準の分野にある他の多くのセキュリティプロジェクトとの間でも、完全でも完全に整合しているわけでもありません。これらの文書の読者は、標準化の過程が進むにつれて、これらの仕様がさまざまな理由で変更される可能性があることを認識しておく必要があります。成し遂げられた作業と、これらの仕様の策定および公開に対する支援について、SDNS プロジェクトの後援者と参加者に謝意を表します。
contents.html: NIST is publishing the specifications that resulted from Phase I of the SDNS project for review and comment from potential government and commercial users of security products. The specifications are not complete or totally consistent, either internally or with a number of other security projects in the National and International Standards arena. Readers of these documents should recognize that these specifications are subject to modification for various reasons as they progress through the standards process. The sponsor and participants in the SDNS project are acknowledged for the work accomplished and their support in developing and releasing these specifications.

contents.html_ja: SDNS プロジェクトは、分散コンピューターネットワークにセキュリティを実装する方法を調査するために NSA が開始しました。このプロジェクトの成果には、OSI コンピューターネットワークモデルに基づくネットワークで利用者データを保護するための、セキュリティサービス、プロトコル、メカニズムを含む一連の仕様が含まれます。利用者データを保護する生産的なセキュリティサービスが規定されているほか、鍵管理やアクセス制御などの支援的なセキュリティサービスも提供されています。これらの仕様には、暗号アルゴリズムは含まれていません。
contents.html: The SDNS project was initiated by NSA to investigate methods of implementing security in a distributed computer network. The results of this project include a set of specifications that include security services, protocols and mechanisms for protecting user data in networks that are based on the OSI computer network model. Productive security services that protect user data are specified and supportive security services, such as key management and access control, are also provided. No cryptographic algorithms are included in these specifications.

contents.html_ja: NISTIR 90-4262 には、鍵管理を扱う 4 つの文書が含まれています。これらは、国家安全保障局（NSA）が、セキュアデータネットワークシステム（SDNS）プロジェクトの成果として作成したものです。SDN.601「SDNS 鍵管理プロトコルをサポートするための通信プロトコル要件」は、オープンシステムにおける SDNS 鍵管理サービスを実装するためのプロファイルを示しています。主として、さまざまな通信固有の環境で鍵管理アプリケーションプロセス（KMAP）の要件を満たすために必要となる多様なプロトコルスタックについて、実装合意のための指針を示すことに関わります。また、さまざまな通信環境、すなわちパケット交換網（PSN）、ローカルエリアネットワーク（LAN）、直接ダイヤルの公衆交換電話網（PSTN）について、トランスポート層、ネットワーク層、データリンク層、物理層で必要となるプロトコルのサポートも規定しています。
contents.html: NISTIR 90-4262 includes four documents dealing with key management which were developed by the National Security Agency (NSA) as output from the Secure Data Network System (SDNS) project. SDN.601, Communication Protocol Requirements for Support of the SDNS Key Management Protocol, supplies a profile for the implementation of SDNS Key Management services in Open Systems. It is primarily concerned with providing guidance for implementation agreements on the variety of protocol stacks that are needed to satisfy the Key Management Application Process (KMAP) requirements in various communication specific environments. It also specifies the protocol support required at the transport, network, data link, and physical layers for varying communication environments; namely Packet Switched Networks (PSN), Local Area Networks (LAN), and direct dial Public Switched Telephone Networks (PSTN).

contents.html_ja: この文書は、オープンシステムにおける SDNS 鍵管理サービスを実装するためのプロファイルを規定します。主として、さまざまな通信固有の環境で鍵管理アプリケーションプロセス（KMAP）の要件を満たすために必要となる多様なプロトコルスタックについて、実装合意のための指針を示すことに関わります。
contents.html: This document specifies a profile for the implementation of SDNS Key Management services in Open Systems. It is primarily concerned with providing guidance for implementation agreements on the variety of protocol stacks that are needed to satisfy the Key Management Application Process (KMAP) requirement in various communication specific environments.

contents.html_ja: 1. 適用範囲と適用分野
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p17 を画像で確認し、OCR の文字を語ごとに照合した。ページの本文を 9 ブロックに組み直す。 節番号 0.〜2. は文字層に無いため画像から補う。「different」の合字、「(GOSIP)」の誤読、行の分断を画像どおりに直す。下端のページ番号「- 5 -」「1」は文字層に無い。

contents.html_ja: このプロファイルは、KMAP がアプリケーション制御サービス要素（ACSE）、ISO プレゼンテーション層カーネル、ISO セッション層に求めるプロトコルサポートサービスを規定します。また、さまざまな通信環境、すなわちパケット交換網（PSN）、ローカルエリアネットワーク（LAN）、直接ダイヤルの公衆交換電話網（PSTN）について、トランスポート層、ネットワーク層、データリンク層、物理層で必要となるプロトコルのサポートも規定します。
contents.html: This profile specifies the protocol support services the KMAP requires from the Application Control Service Elements (ACSE), the ISO Presentation layer kernel, and the ISO Session layer. It also specifies the protocol support required at the transport, network, data link, and physical layers for varying communication environments; namely, Packet Switched Networks (PSN), Local Area Networks (LAN), and direct dial Public Switched Telephone Networks (PSTN).

contents.html_ja: 以下の段落で参照するプロトコルは、鍵管理機能を実行する際に使用する、ISO の第 7 層から第 5 層までの基本的なコネクション型メッセージトラフィックを提供するために必要です。第 4 層以下では、想定されるさまざまな SDNS のコネクション型およびコネクションレス型の環境をサポートするために、いくつかの異なる選択肢が利用できます。
contents.html: The protocols referenced in the following paragraphs are required to provide the basic connection oriented message traffic, at ISO layers seven through five, for use in performing key management functions. At layer four and below, several different options are available to support a variety of envisioned SDNS connection and connectionless oriented environments.

contents.html_ja: KMAP のプロトコルスタックの代替案を図 1 に示します。図 1 に示すとおり、KMASE は常に、ISO 第 7 層の ACSE、ISO 第 6 層のプレゼンテーションカーネル、第 5 層の ISO セッションプロトコルのサービスを必要とします。プレゼンテーション層およびセッション層のプロトコルは、米国政府の利用向けに開発された SDNS コンポーネントについて ISO 標準を補足する、政府開放型システム間相互接続プロファイル（GOSIP）標準に従って実装しなければなりません。
contents.html: The KMAP protocol stack alternatives are depicted in Figure 1. As illustrated in figure 1, the KMASE always requires the services of the ISO layer 7 ACSE, the ISO layer 6 Presentation kernel, and the ISO Session Protocol, at layer 5. The Presentation and Session layer protocols shall be implemented in accordance with Government Open System Interconnection Profile (GOSIP) standards, which supplement ISO standards for SDNS components developed for U.S. Government use.

contents.html_ja: 国防総省（DoD）の伝送制御プロトコル（TCP）およびインターネットプロトコル（IP）の実装では、ISO セッション層を DoD トランスポート層にマッピングしなければなりません。このマッピングの詳細は、この文書の範囲外です。
contents.html: For Department of Defense (DoD) Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and Internet Protocol (IP) implementations, the ISO Session layer must be mapped to the DoD Transport layer. The specifics of this mapping are beyond the scope of this document.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p17 を画像で確認し、OCR の文字を語ごとに照合した。ページの本文を 9 ブロックに組み直す。 節番号 0.〜2. は文字層に無いため画像から補う。「different」の合字、「(GOSIP)」の誤読、行の分断を画像どおりに直す。下端のページ番号「- 5 -」「1」は文字層に無い。

contents.html_ja: 直接ダイヤルの PSTN 接続が必要な場合、トランスポート層は ISO TP クラス 0 を使用します。SDNS 鍵管理のサポートでは、TP(0) は「パブリックドメイン」の X.PC 仕様とあわせてのみ使用します。SDNS 鍵管理のサポートに ISO コネクションレスネットワークプロトコル（CLNP）を使用する場合、トランスポート層には ISO TP クラス 4 が必要です。コネクションレスのネットワーク層で DoD のインターネットプロトコル（IP）を使用する場合、トランスポート層には DoD の TCP を使用しなければなりません。DoD の TCP の使用は、上述のとおり、ISO セッション層からの標準的なマッピング規約に依存します。
contents.html: The Transport layer will use ISO TP class 0 when direct dial PSTN connections are required. For SDNS key management support, TP(0) will only be used in conjunction with the "public domain” X.PC specification. The Transport layer requires ISO TP class 4 when the ISO Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP) is employed for SDNS key management support. The DoD’s TCP must be used for the transport layer when the DoD Internet Protocol (IP) is employed at the connectionless network layer. The use of DoD’s TCP is dependent upon a standard mapping convention from the ISO Session layer, as stated above.

contents.html: At the Network layer, the ISO CLNP standard is employed when ISO TP(4) is utilized at the Transport layer. CLNP may interface to X.25 layer 3, or to the Data Link layer for broadcast LANs (IEEE 802 standards). The DoD IP connectionless network protocol is used when DoD TCP is utilized at the Transport layer. IP may interconnect to an underlying X.25 layer 3, or to the data link layer for LANs using IEEE 802 standards.
contents.html_ja: ネットワーク層では、トランスポート層で ISO TP(4) を使用する場合に、ISO CLNP 標準を用います。CLNP は、X.25 の第 3 層、またはブロードキャスト LAN（IEEE 802 標準）のデータリンク層とインターフェースしてもよいです。トランスポート層で DoD TCP を使用する場合には、DoD IP コネクションレスネットワークプロトコルを用います。IP は、基盤となる X.25 の第 3 層、または IEEE 802 標準を使用する LAN のデータリンク層と相互接続してもよいです。

contents.html_ja: ACSE は ISO 8650/2 に規定されています。すべての特定アプリケーションサービス要素（SASE）、すなわち ISO アプリケーション層における KMASE のようなものは、ピアの SASE とのコネクションの確立、解放、中止に ACSE を使用します。ISO 標準に規定されているすべての ACSE プロトコルデータユニット（APDU）の種類とサービスプリミティブは、すべての SDNS 鍵管理アプリケーションで必要です。
contents.html: ACSE is specified in ISO 8650/2. All Specific Application Service Elements (SASE) - i.e., what the KMASE is in the ISO application layer, use ACSE to establish, release, and abort connections with peer SASE. All ACSE Protocol Data Unit (APDU) types and service primitives specified in the ISO standard are required for all SDNS key management applications.

contents.html_ja: コネクション型のプレゼンテーションプロトコル（PP）は、APDU および KPDU の情報内容が、アプリケーションエンティティ間の伝送中に保持されることを保証するために存在します。PP が行う機能には、転送構文のネゴシエーションと、転送構文への変換および転送構文からの変換が含まれます。サービスには、コネクションの確立と解放、コンテキスト管理、情報転送が含まれます。連携する SDNS 機器は、KPDU に単一の転送構文を使用しなければなりません。
contents.html: Connection oriented Presentation protocols (PP) exist to ensure that the information content of APDUs and KPDUs are preserved during their transit between application entities. Functions performed by PP include negotiation of transfer syntaxes and transformation to/from transfer syntax. Services include connection establishment and release, context management, and information transfer. Cooperating SDNS devices shall use a single transfer syntax for KPDUs.

contents.html_ja: 連携する SDNS 実装は、セッションカーネル、全二重、緊急データの各機能単位が使用するすべての SPDU の種類とプリミティブをサポートしなければなりません。各機能単位について、すべての必須パラメーターをサポートしなければなりません。機能単位と SPDU パラメーターの詳細は、ISO 8327 に定義されています。サポートされないパラメーターオプションがあっても、プロトコルエラーになったり PDU が破棄されたりしてはなりません。
contents.html: Cooperating SDNS implementations shall support all SPDU types and primitives used by the session kernel, duplex, and expedited data functional units. Unsupported parameter options shall not result in a protocol error or PDU discard.

contents.html: TP(4) shall be implemented when the underlying network protocol is the ISO Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP). All mandatory parameters for TPDUs shall be implemented, as defined in ISO 8073 and DIS 8073/AD2. Unsupported parameter options shall not result in a protocol error or PDU discard.

contents.html_ja: 「ダイヤルアップ」アクセスモードでのすべての SDNS 鍵管理のやり取りをサポートするには、TP(0) が必要です。このアクセスモードでは、X.PC「公開」プロトコルの基盤サービスが必要です。TP0 の TPDU とセッションプロトコルのプリミティブの詳細は、ISO 8073 に定義されています。連携する TP0 実装は、すべての TPDU とセッションプロトコルのプリミティブ、およびすべての必須パラメーターをサポートしなければなりません。サポートされないオプションパラメーターがあっても、プロトコルエラーになったり PDU が破棄されたりしてはなりません。
contents.html: TP(0) is required to support all SDNS key management exchanges in the "dial-up" access mode. This access mode requires the underlying services of the X.PC "public domain" protocol. Unsupported optional parameters shall not result in a protocol error or PDU discard.

contents.html_ja: すでに多数の IP ルーターが存在するインターネットワーク内で動作せざるを得ない SDNS 鍵管理のやり取りをサポートするには、TCP が必要です。この種の実装は推奨されませんが、SDNS コンポーネントの配備費用を最小限に抑えるために必要となる場合があります。たとえば、SDNS 機器を配備するネットワークで利用できるルーターが IP ルーターだけである場合です。ISO セッション層から DoD トランスポート層へのプロトコルマッピングが標準化されるまでは、この種の一貫した実装は実現可能でない場合があります。
contents.html: TCP is required to support SDNS key management exchanges that are compelled to operate within internets that already exist with a significant number of IP routers. This kind of implementation is not encouraged, but may be necessary in some cases to keep the cost of deploying SDNS components to a minimum; for example, where IP routers are the only available routers on networks where SDNS devices are to be deployed. Consistent implementations of this type may not be feasible until ISO Session layer to DoD transport layer protocol mappings are standardized.

contents.html: The X.PC "public domain" protocol shall be used for all key management exchanges that are required over direct dial PSTNs. contents.html_ja: この節では、鍵管理アプリケーションサービス要素（KMASE）が提供する鍵管理サービスを定義します。定義されるサービスは、特定アプリケーションサービス要素（SASE）のカテゴリに属します。これらのサービスは、連携する鍵管理アプリケーションプロセス（KMAP）が必要とする鍵管理活動、およびその活動を支援する機能を提供します。これには、トラフィック暗号化鍵（TEK）の確立、TEK の更新、証明書失効リスト（CRL）の配布、ならびに鍵管理システム（KMS）との対話型および段階的な再鍵（rekey）が含まれます。
contents.html: This section defines the key management services as provided by the Key Management Application Service Element (KMASE). The services defined are of the category Specific Application Service Element (SASE). It provides facilities to support the key management activities required by and in support of cooperating Key Management Application Processes (KMAP) including the establishment of traffic encryption keys (TEK), the updating of TEKs, the distribution of Certificate Revocation Lists (CRL), and the interactive and staged rekey with the Key Management System (KMS).

contents.html: This standard only defines the services in terms of an abstract model. contents.html: This part of the KMP specification uses the descriptive conventions in the OSI Service Conventions in ISO/TR 8509. contents.html_ja: このサービス定義は、ISO TR 8509 の OSI サービス規約に定義されたサービスの抽象モデルを用います。このモデルは、連携する 2 つの KMAP の間の相互作用を定義します。KMAP は、情報処理部と、KMAE で表される通信部の 2 つの部分から構成されます。2 つの KMAP の間で通信が必要になると、それらのプロセスの KMAE の呼び出しの間にアプリケーションアソシエーションが確立されます。KMAE は、KMASE と ACSE によって定義される、アドレス指定可能な通信機能の集合を表します。
contents.html: This service definition uses the abstract model for a service defined in the OSI Service Conventions in ISO TR 8509. The model defines the interactions between two cooperating KMAPs. The KMAP consists of two parts: the information processing part, and the communication part, which is represented by the KMAE. When communication is required between two KMAPs, an application association is established between invocations of the processes’ KMAEs. The KMAE represents an addressable set of communication capabilities which are defined by the KMASE and the ACSE.

contents.html_ja: K-DELIVER-SREKEY サービスは、再鍵エージェントが、K-REQUEST-SREKEY サービスを使用して以前に段階的再鍵を要求したコンポーネントに、鍵素材を配送できるようにします。
contents.html: The K-DELIVER-SREKEY service enables a Rekey Agent to deliver key material to a component which has previously requested a staged rekey by the use of the K-REQUEST-SREKEY service.

contents.html_ja: K-GET-CRL サービスは、KMAP が、連携する KMAP（たとえば KMS の KMAP）から CRL を入手できるようにします。新しい CRL が配送されるのは、要求側が、応答側よりも古い版の CRL を持っている場合だけです。
contents.html: The K-GET-CRL service enables a KMAP to obtain a CRL from a cooperating KMAP (e.g. the KMS KMAP). The new CRL is delivered only if the requestor has an older version of the CRL than the responder.

contents.html_ja: KMASE は、特定アプリケーションサービス要素です。ここに規定されているとおり、完全な通信サービスを記述するものではなく、アソシエーション制御サービス要素（ACSE）に依存します。KMASE は、ACSE によって制御される既存のアプリケーションアソシエーションを必要とします。また KMASE は、ピアの SDNS エンティティ間で SDNS 鍵管理メッセージを転送するために、プレゼンテーションサービスの P-DATA サービスを使用することを想定しています。
contents.html: The KMASE is a specific application service element. As specified here it does not describe a complete communications service, but instead relies on the Association Control Service Element (ACSE). The KMASE requires an existing application-association controlled by ACSE. The KMASE also assumes the use of the P-DATA service of the Presentation Service for transferring SDNS key management messages between peer SDNS entities.

It is a confirmed service.

contents.html_ja: 鍵管理プロトコルには、連携する KMAE 間で KMP KPDU の形式の情報を受け渡すための転送サービスが必要です。このサービスは KMASE が提供します。この仕様は、ACSE によって確立・解放される既存のアプリケーションアソシエーションを前提としています。この仕様で定義する鍵管理プロトコルは、コネクション型プレゼンテーションサービス（ISO DIS 8822）と ACSE サービス（ISO DIS 8649）の使用を前提としています。
contents.html: The Key Management Protocol needs a transfer service to pass information in the form of KMP KPDUs between cooperating KMAEs. This service is provided by the KMASE. This specification assumes an existing application association, established and released by means of ACSE. The Key Management Protocol defined in this specification assumes the use of the connection-oriented presentation services (ISO DIS 8822) and the ACSE services (ISO DIS 8649).

contents.html_ja: KMAP は、情報処理部と、KMAE で表される通信部の 2 つの部分から構成されます。2 つの KMAP の間で通信が必要になると、それらのプロセスの KMAE の呼び出しの間にアプリケーションアソシエーションが確立されます。KMAE は、KMASE と ACSE によって定義される、アドレス指定可能な通信機能の集合を表します。
contents.html: The KMAP comprises two parts: the information processor part and the communication part represented by the KMAE. When communication is required between two KMAPs, an application association is established between invocations of the processes’ KMAEs. The KMAE represents an addressable set of communication capabilities which are defined by the KMASE and the ACSE.

contents.html_ja: KMASE サービスの使用中は、連携する KMAE 間にアプリケーションアソシエーションが存在することが前提となります。アプリケーションアソシエーション上の通信の性質と目的は、そのために確立された情報処理コンテキストとアプリケーションコンテキストによって決まります。
contents.html: During the use of the KMASE services, the existence of an application association between cooperating KMAEs is presumed. The nature and purpose of communication over the application association are determined by the information processing context and the application context which are established for it.

contents.html_ja: KMASE は、KMAP からのサービス要求プリミティブと応答プリミティブ、およびプレゼンテーションサービスプロバイダーからの通知プリミティブによって駆動されます。KMASE は、これを受けて、KMAP に通知プリミティブと確認プリミティブを発行し、ACSE とプレゼンテーションサービスプロバイダーに要求プリミティブを発行します。
contents.html: The KMASE is driven by service request and response primitives from the KMAP and by indication primitives from the presentation service provider. contents.html_ja: KMAP は、K-MIB と TEK-MIB を管理します。これは、通知と確認を受け取ったときに IB のデータを更新し、要求と応答を発行するときに IB からパラメーターを取り出すという意味です。K-MIB は、鍵素材を保存するために使われるセキュリティ MIB です。TEK-MIB は、TEK、鍵識別子（KID）、および TEK の使用に関する属性を保存するために使われるセキュリティ MIB です。
contents.html: The KMAP administers the K-MIB and the TEK-MIB in the sense of updating data in the IB upon receipt of indications and confirms and retrieving parameters from the IB when issuing requests and responses. K-MIB is a security MIB used to store key material. TEK-MIB is a security MIB used to store TEK, key identifiers (KIDs) and attributes regarding the use of the TEK.

contents.html_ja: TEK を確立するために必要なクレデンシャルは、一方の KMASE（イニシエーター）が Nkrq KPDU をもう一方の KMASE（レスポンダー）に送信し、レスポンダーが Nkrs KPDU で返信することによって交換されます。
contents.html: The credentials required to establish a TEK are exchanged by one KMASE (the initiator) transmitting a Nkrq KPDU to the other KMASE (the responder), which replies with a Nkrs KPDU.

contents.html_ja: イニシエーター KMASE は、K-EXCH-CRED 要求プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して、Nkrq KPDU を組み立てます。この KPDU には、新しい TEK についてのイニシエーターの KID（init-kid）、ユニバーサル ID（univ-id）、およびイニシエーターのクレデンシャル（init-cred）が含まれます。この Nkrq KPDU は、レスポンダー KMASE に送信されます。
contents.html: The initiator KMASE uses the parameters from the K-EXCH-CRED request primitive to build a Nkrq KPDU. This KPDU contains the initiator's KID for the new TEK (init-kid), the universal-ID (univ-id), and the initiator's credentials (init-cred). This Nkrq KPDU is sent to the responder KMASE.

contents.html_ja: Nkrq を受信すると、レスポンダー KMASE は KMAP に K-EXCH-CRED 通知プリミティブを発行します。レスポンダー KMASE は、これ以降、レスポンダーの KID とレスポンダーのクレデンシャルを含む K-EXCH-CRED 応答プリミティブが KMAP から届くのを待ちます。
contents.html: On receipt of an Nkrq, the responder KMASE issues a K-EXCH-CRED indication primitive to the KMAP. The responder KMASE now expects a K-EXCH-CRED response primitive from the KMAP containing the responder KID and the responder's credentials.

contents.html_ja: レスポンダー KMASE は、パラメーターが交換の成功を示している場合、K-EXCH-CRED 応答プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して Nkrs KPDU を作成します。この KPDU には、新しい TEK についてのイニシエーターの KID（init-kid）、新しい TEK についてのレスポンダーの KID（resp-kid）、およびレスポンダーのクレデンシャル（resp-cred）が含まれます。Nkrs KPDU は、イニシエーター KMASE に送信されます。K-EXCH-CRED 応答プリミティブが失敗の結果を示している場合、レスポンダー KMASE は ACSE に A-ABORT 要求プリミティブを発行します。
contents.html: The responder KMASE uses the parameters from the K-EXCH-CRED response primitive to prepare a Nkrs KPDU, when the parameters indicate a successful exchange. This KPDU contains the initiator’s KID for the new TEK (init-kid), the responder’s KID for the new TEK (resp-kid), and the responder’s credentials (resp-cred). The Nkrs KPDU is sent to the initiator KMASE. If the K-EXCH-CRED response primitive indicates a failure result, the responder KMASE issues an A-ABORT request primitive to the ACSE.

contents.html_ja: セキュリティ属性と通信属性は、一方の KMASE（イニシエーター）が Ssrq KPDU をもう一方の KMASE（レスポンダー）に送信し、レスポンダーが Ssrs KPDU で返信することによってネゴシエーションされます。イニシエーターは、ネゴシエーション可能な通信およびセキュリティのパラメーターオプションのセットの一覧を、Ssrq KPDU で指定します。レスポンダーは、選択したオプションのセットを Ssrs KPDU で指定します。
contents.html: Security and communication attributes are negotiated by means of one KMASE (the initiator) transmitting a Ssrq KPDU to the other KMASE (the responder), which replies with a Ssrs KPDU. The initiator specifies a list of sets of negotiable communication and security parameter options in the Ssrq KPDU. The responder specifies the selected set of options in the Ssrs KPDU.
contents.extraction_note: 原本画像と文字層で照合（Claude Opus）。原本p64 を画像で確認し、OCR の文字を語ごとに照合した。ページの本文を 19 ブロックに組み直す。 KPDU と引数の箇条、分断された段落、「KID (old-resp-kid)」を画像どおりに組み直す。最後の段落は p65 に続く（文字層の b0018 は p65 の続きを含む。p65 の画像で確認）。

contents.html_ja: イニシエーター KMASE は、K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES 要求プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して、Ssrq KPDU を作成します。Ssrq KPDU には、旧レスポンダー KID（old-resp-kid）、イニシエーターの CRL バージョン番号（crl-ver）、オプションセット（proposed-options）、および追加情報（add-info）が含まれます。オプションセットには、イニシエーターが許容するすべてのオプションのセットが含まれます。オプションセットの優先順位は、並び順の先頭から末尾への優先順位で決まります。Ssrq KPDU を形成した後、イニシエーター KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化します。icv と暗号化の両方に使用される暗号鍵は、先に形成された TEK です。KMASE は、EKpdu をレスポンダー KMASE に送信します。
contents.html: The initiator KMASE uses the parameters from the K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES request primitive to prepare a Ssrq KPDU. The Ssrq KPDU contains the old responder KID (old-resp-kid), the initiator's CRL version number (crl-ver), option sets (proposed-options), and additional information (add-info). Option sets contain all sets of options that the initiator will allow. Option set preference is determined by first-to-last precedence in the ordering. After forming the Ssrq KPDU, the initiator KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, and encodes the result into the EKpdu format. The cryptographic key used for both the icv and the encryption is the previously formed TEK. The KMASE sends the EKpdu to the responder KMASE.

contents.html_ja: EKpdu を受信すると、レスポンダー KMASE は、EKpdu の復号と icv の検証を行います。どちらかの操作が失敗した場合、KMASE は ACSE に A-ABORT 要求プリミティブを発行します。復号と icv の検証の両方が成功した場合、KMASE は、レスポンダー KMAP に K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES 通知プリミティブを発行します。KMASE は、これ以降、K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES 応答プリミティブを待ちます。
contents.html: On receipt of a EKpdu, the responder KMASE performs the EKpdu decryption and icv verification. If either operation fails, the KMASE issues an A-ABORT request primitive to the ACSE. If both decryption and icv verification are successful, the KMASE issues a K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES indication primitive to the responder KMAP. The KMASE now expects a K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES response primitive.

contents.html_ja: レスポンダー KMASE は、パラメーターが属性ネゴシエーションの成功を示している場合、K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES 応答プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して Ssrs KPDU を作成します。Ssrs KPDU には、レスポンダーの CRL バージョン番号（crl-ver）、オプションセット（selected-options）、および追加情報（add-info）が含まれます。オプションセットには、Ssrq にあるイニシエーターのセットから選ばれた、通信およびセキュリティのオプションパラメーターのセットが含まれます。Ssrs KPDU を形成した後、KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、イニシエーター KMASE に送信します。icv と暗号化の両方に使用される暗号鍵は、先に形成された TEK です。K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES 応答プリミティブのパラメーターが属性ネゴシエーション操作の失敗を示している場合、レスポンダー KMASE は、Ssrs KPDU の代わりに Estat KPDU を作成します。Estat KPDU には、ステータス（estatus）が含まれます。失敗の原因が service-not-available-at-this-time（現時点ではサービスを利用できない）である場合は、イニシエーター KMAP が要求を再試行すべき最も早い時刻（doNotTryBefore）が含まれます。Estat KPDU を形成した後、レスポンダー KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、イニシエーター KMASE に送信します。
contents.html: The responder KMASE uses the parameters from the K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES response primitive to prepare a Ssrs KPDU when the parameters indicate successful attribute negotiation. The Ssrs KPDU contains the responder's CRL version number (crl-ver), option set (selected-options), and additional information (add-info). The Option Set contains the set of communication and security option parameters chosen from the initiator's sets in the Ssrq. After forming the Ssrs KPDU, the KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format and sends it to the initiator KMASE. The cryptographic key used for both the icv and the encryption is the previously formed TEK. If the parameters of the K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES response primitive indicate a failure of the attribute negotiation operation, the responder KMASE prepares an Estat KPDU instead of the Ssrs KPDU. The Estat KPDU contains a status (estatus). When the failure is service-not-available-at-this-time, the earliest time the initiator KMAP should attempt the request again is included (doNotTryBefore). After forming the Estat KPDU, the responder KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format, and sends it to the initiator KMASE.

After forming the Kurq KPDU, the KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format. contents.html: The responder KMASE uses the parameters from the K-UPDATE-TEK response primitive to prepare a Kurs KPDU, when the K-UPDATE-TEK response primitive indicates that the key update operation is successful. If the K-UPDATE-TEK response primitive indicates a failure of the key update operation, the responder KMASE issues an A-ABORT request primitive to the ACSE.

contents.html_ja: イニシエーター KMASE は、K-IREKEY 要求プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して、Rkrq KPDU を作成します。この KPDU には、置き換える鍵素材に関連付けられたユニバーサル ID（univ-id）と、イニシエーター SDNS コンポーネントが保持していてそのユニバーサル ID に関連付けられた現在の CRL バージョン番号（crl-ver）が含まれます。イニシエーターが再鍵エージェントである場合、Rkrq KPDU には、再鍵されるクレデンシャル（rekey-cred）が含まれてもよいです。コンポーネントが電子鍵交換を予定している場合、ekr パラメーター（ekr）は TRUE に設定されます。さらに、これが段階的再鍵手順の第 2 部である場合、Rkrq KPDU には参照番号（ref-num）が含まれます。Rkrq KPDU を形成した後、イニシエーター KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、KMS KMASE に送信します。
contents.html: The initiator KMASE uses the parameters from the K-IREKEY request primitive to prepare a Rkrq KPDU. This KPDU contains the universal-ID associated with the key material to be replaced (univ-id), and the current CRL version number held by the initiator SDNS component and associated with the universal-ID (crl-ver). If the initiator is a rekey agent, the Rkrq KPDU may also contain the credentials to be rekeyed (rekey-cred). If the component is expecting an electronic key replacement, the ekr parameter (ekr) is set to TRUE . Additionally, if this is the second part of a staged rekey procedure, the Rkrq KPDU contains the reference number (ref-num). After forming the Rkrq KPDU, the initiator KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format and sends it to the KMS KMASE.

If both decryption and icv verification are successful, the KMS KMASE issues a K-IREKEY indication primitive to the KMS KMAP. The KMS KMASE now expects a K-IREKEY response primitive.

contents.html_ja: KMS KMASE は、再鍵操作が成功した場合、K-IREKEY 応答プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して Rkrs KPDU を作成します。この KPDU には、KMS のクレデンシャル（kms-cred-A と kms-cred-B）、新しい鍵素材（new-k-mat-A と new-k-mat-B）、およびこの再鍵が行われたユニバーサル ID に関連付けられた KMS の現在の CRL バージョン番号（crl-ver）が含まれます。CRL のバージョンがイニシエーターの CRL バージョンより新しい場合、Rkrs には、KMS が署名した新しい CRL（new-crl）も含まれます。コンポーネントが電子鍵交換も受け取る場合、ekr パラメーター（ekr）は TRUE に設定されます。さらに、これが段階的再鍵手順の第 2 部である場合、Rkrs KPDU には参照識別子（ref-num）が含まれます。この再鍵プロセスがユニバーサル再鍵である場合、Rkrs KPDU には、new-k-mat フィールド（new-k-mat-A と new-k-mat-B）に新しいユニバーサル鍵素材と、新しいユニバーサルの CRL（new-univ-crl）も含まれます。任意で、Rkrs KPDU には、KMS がこの時点でこのアソシエーションでそれ以上の再鍵要求を受け付けられないことを示すフラグ（no-more）が含まれてもよいです。Rkrs KPDU を形成した後、KMS KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、イニシエーター KMASE に送信します。K-IREKEY 応答プリミティブが対話型再鍵操作の失敗を示している場合、KMS KMASE は、Rkrs KPDU の代わりに Estat KPDU を作成します。Estat KPDU には、ステータス（estatus）が含まれます。失敗の原因が service-not-available-at-this-time（現時点ではサービスを利用できない）である場合は、イニシエーター KMAP が要求を再試行すべき最も早い時刻（doNotTryBefore）が含まれます。Estat KPDU を形成した後、レスポンダー KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、イニシエーター KMASE に送信します。
contents.html: The KMS KMASE uses the parameters from the K-IREKEY response primitive to prepare a Rkrs KPDU, when the rekey operation is successful. This KPDU contains the KMS credentials (kms-cred-A and kms-cred-B), the new key material (new-k-mat-A and new-k-mat-B), and the current KMS CRL version number associated with the universal-ID under which this rekey was performed (crl-ver). If the CRL version is more recent than the initiator's CRL version, the Rkrs also contains the new CRL signed by the KMS (new-crl). If the component is also receiving an electronic key replacement, the ekr parameter (ekr) is set to TRUE. Additionally, if this is the second part of a staged rekey procedure, the Rkrs KPDU contains the reference identifier (ref-num). If this rekey process is a universal rekey, the Rkrs KPDU also contains the new universal key material in the new-k-mat fields (new-k-mat-A and new-k-mat-B) and CRL of the new universal (new-univ-crl). Optionally, the Rkrs KPDU may contain a flag to indicate that the KMS cannot accept any further rekey requests on this association at this time (no-more). After forming the Rkrs KPDU, the KMS KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format and sends it to the initiator KMASE. If the K-IREKEY response primitive indicates a failure of the interactive rekey operation, the KMS KMASE prepares a Estat KPDU instead of a Rkrs KPDU. The Estat KPDU contains a status (estatus). When the failure is service-not-available-at-this-time, the earliest time the initiator KMAP should attempt the request again is included (doNotTryBefore). After forming the Estat KPDU, the responder KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format and sends it to the initiator KMASE.

contents.html_ja: イニシエーター KMASE は、K-REQUEST-SREKEY 要求プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して、Srkrq KPDU を作成します。Srkrq KPDU には、置き換える鍵素材に関連付けられたユニバーサル ID（univ-id）と、イニシエーター SDNS コンポーネントが保持していてそのユニバーサル ID に関連付けられた現在の CRL バージョン番号（crl-ver）が含まれます。さらに、Srkrq KPDU には、KMS が再鍵操作を行う際に使用すべきクレデンシャル（rekey-cred）と、イニシエーターが電子鍵交換を期待しているかどうかの通知（ekr）が含まれます。Srkrq KPDU を形成した後、イニシエーター KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、レスポンダー KMASE に送信します。
contents.html: The initiator KMASE uses the parameters from the K-REQUEST-SREKEY request primitive to prepare a Srkrq KPDU. The Srkrq KPDU contains the universal-ID associated with the key material to be replaced (univ-id) and the current CRL version number held by the initiator SDNS component and associated with the universal-ID (crl-ver). Additionally, the Srkrq KPDU contains the credentials that the KMS should use to perform the rekey operation (rekey-cred) and a notification of whether the initiator expects an electronic key replacement (ekr). After forming the Srkrq KPDU, the initiator KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format and sends it to the responder KMASE.

contents.html: If the K-REQUEST-SREKEY response primitive indicates a failure, the Rekey Agent KMASE prepares a Estat KPDU instead of a Srkrs KPDU. The Estat KPDU contains a status (estatus). After forming the Estat KPDU, the responder KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format and sends it to the initiator KMASE.

contents.html_ja: 再鍵エージェント KMASE は、K-DELIVER-SREKEY 応答プリミティブが操作の成功を示している場合、その応答プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して Srdrs KPDU を作成します。Srdrs KPDU には、KMS のクレデンシャル（kms-cred-A と kms-cred-B）、新しい鍵素材（new-k-mat-A と new-k-mat-B）が含まれます。また、KMS が再鍵操作を実行した時点で universal-ID に関連付けられていた現在の CRL バージョン番号（crl-ver）も含まれます。新しい CRL（new-crl）も含まれる場合があります。さらに、Srdrs KPDU には、イニシエーターが電子鍵交換を受け取ったかどうかの通知（ekr）が含まれます。この再鍵プロセスがユニバーサル再鍵である場合、Rkrs KPDU には、new-k-mat フィールド（new-k-mat-A と new-k-mat-B）内の新しいユニバーサル鍵素材と、新しいユニバーサルの CRL（new-univ-crl）も含まれます。Srdrs KPDU を形成した後、レスポンダー KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、イニシエーター KMASE に送信します。
contents.html: The Rekey Agent KMASE uses the parameters from the K-DELIVER-SREKEY reponse primitive to prepare a Srdrs KPDU, when the K-DELIVER-SREKEY response primitive indicates a successful operation. The Srdrs KPDU contains the KMS credentials (kms-cred-A and kms-cred-B), the new key material (new-k-mat-A and new-k-mat-B). Also, the Srdrs KPDU contains the current crl version number associated with the universal-ID at the time the KMS performed the rekey operation (crl-ver). The new CRL (new-crl) may also be present. Additionally, the Srdrs KPDU contains a notification as to whether the initiator received an electronic key replacement (ekr). If this rekey process is a universal rekey, the Rkrs KPDU also contains the new universal key material in the new-k-mat fields (new-k-mat-A and new-k-mat-B) and CRL of the new universal (new-univ-crl). After forming the Srdrs KPDU, the responder KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format and sends it to the initiator KMASE.

contents.html_ja: イニシエーター KMASE は、K-GET-CRL 要求プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して、Crrq KPDU を作成します。Crrq KPDU には、イニシエーターの crl のバージョン番号（crl-ver）が含まれます。Crrq KPDU を形成した後、イニシエーター KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、レスポンダー KMASE に送信します。icv と暗号化の両方に使用される暗号鍵は、先に形成された TEK です。
contents.html: The initiator KMASE uses the parameters from the K-GET-CRL request primitive to prepare a Crrq KPDU. The Crrq KPDU contains the version number of the initiator’s crl (crl-ver). After forming the Crrq KPDU, the initiator KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format and sends it to the responder KMASE. The cryptographic key used for both the icv and the encryption is the previously formed TEK.

contents.html: When the responder KMASE receives the EKpdu, it performs the EKpdu decryption and icv verification. If either operation fails, the responder KMASE issues an A-ABORT request primitive to the ACSE. If both decryption and icv verification are successful, the KMASE issues a K-GET-CRL indication primitive to the responder KMAP. The responder KMASE now expects a K-GET-CRL response primitive.

contents.html_ja: レスポンダー KMASE は、K-GET-CRL のパラメーターが操作の成功を示している場合、K-GET-CRL 応答プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して Crrs KPDU を作成します。Crrs KPDU には、レスポンダー SDNS コンポーネントが保持する（現在の TEK に関連付けられたユニバーサルの）現在の署名付き CRL（new-crl）、またはイニシエーターの CRL バージョンが最新である場合は CRL バージョン番号（currentcrl）のいずれかが含まれます。Crrs KPDU を形成した後、レスポンダー KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、イニシエーター KMASE に送信します。K-GET-CRL 応答プリミティブが CRL 取得操作の失敗（たとえば、レスポンダーが現時点で CRL を提供できない、または CRL の交換をサポートしていない場合）を示している場合、レスポンダー KMASE は、Crrs KPDU の代わりに Estat KPDU を作成します。Estat KPDU には、ステータス（estatus）が含まれます。失敗の原因が service-not-available-at-this-time（現時点ではサービスを利用できない）である場合は、イニシエーター KMAP が再び要求を試みるべき最も早い時刻（doNotTryBefore）が含まれます。Estat KPDU を形成した後、レスポンダー KMASE は、その KPDU を PlainText Kpdu の形式に符号化し、PlainText Kpdu を暗号化し、その結果を EKpdu の形式に符号化して、イニシエーター KMASE に送信します。
contents.html: The responder KMASE uses the parameters from the K-GET-CRL response primitive to prepare a Crrs KPDU, when the K-GET-CRL parameters indicate a successful operation. The Crrs KPDU contains either the current signed CRL (for the universal associated with the current TEK) held by the responder SDNS component (new-crl) or the CRL version number (currentcrl) if the initiator’s CRL version is current. After forming the Crrs KPDU, the responder KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format, and sends it to the initiator KMASE. If the K-GET-CRL response primitive indicates a failure of the get CRL operation (e.g. the responder cannot supply the CRL at this time, or does not support CRL exchanges), the responder KMASE prepares a Estat KPDU instead of a Crrs KPDU. The Estat KPDU contains a status (estatus). When the failure is service-not-available-at-this-time, the earliest time the initiator KMAP should attempt the request again is included (doNotTryBefore). After forming the Estat KPDU, the responder KMASE encodes the KPDU into the PlainText Kpdu format, encrypts the PlainText Kpdu, encodes the result into the EKpdu format and sends it to the initiator KMASE.

contents.html_ja: この節は、鍵管理プロトコルが交換する PDU を定義するために、DIS 8824「Specification of Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1)」に規定された抽象構文記法 1（Abstract Syntax Notation One）を用います。これは、この型のインスタンスが転送中にどのように（オクテット列によって）表現されるかを決定することなく行われます。符号化規則は、抽象構文で定義された型の転送構文を生成するために使用されます。以下の抽象構文の転送構文に使用する符号化規則は、DIS 8825「Specification of Basic Encoding Rules for ASN.1」に規定されています。
contents.html: This section uses the Abstract Syntax Notation One specified in DIS 8824, Specification of Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.1), to define the PDUs exchanged by the key management protocol. This is done without determining the way an instance of this type is to be represented (by a sequence of octets) during transfer. Encoding rules are used to produce a transfer syntax for the types defined in the abstract syntax. The Encoding Rules to be used for the transfer syntax of the following Abstract Syntax are specified in DIS 8825, Specification of Basic Encoding Rules for ASN.1.

BEGIN

IMPORTS

Universal-id           :: = [APPLICATION 26] IMPLICIT INTEGER

-- Encrypted PDU's. Each has a KID in plaintext

EKpdu :: = SEQUENCE {
remote-kid KeyId,
-- remote-kid is either init-kid or resp-kid depending on decrypted contents
contents OCTET STRING  -- ENCRYPTED PlainText Kpdu
}

--The contents of an encrypted PDU.

PlainTextKpdu :: = SEQUENCE {
-- must not be encoded with indefinite length
plaintext CHOICE {
[0] IMPLICIT Ssrq,
[1] IMPLICIT Ssrs,
result        [2] IMPLICIT Estat,
[3] IMPLICIT Kurq,
[4] IMPLICIT Kurs,
[5] IMPLICIT Rkrq,
[6] IMPLICIT Rkrs,
[7] IMPLICIT Srkrq,
[8] IMPLICIT Srkrs,
[9] IMPLICIT Srdrq,
[10] IMPLICIT Srdrs,
[11] IMPLICIT Crrq,
[12]            Crrs
},
padding OCTET STRING OPTIONAL,
icv IntegrityCheckValue
} --Note icv is guaranteed to be last.
--Note Indefinite length encoding of icv is prohibited.

-- Security Services Request

Ssrq :: =  SET {
crl-ver              Crl-Ver,
NewOrOldOptions,
add-info             AddInfo OPTIONAL
},
NewOrOldOptions :: =  CHOICE {
old-resp-kid         KeyId ,
proposed-options     SEQUENCE OF AttributeSet ,
-- ordered by preference
} --Note AttributeSet and AddInfo will be imported. See SDN.906, SDNS Traffic Key Attribute Negotiation.

-- Security Services Response

Ssrs :: = SET {
crl-ver                  Crl-Ver,
selected-options         [0] AttributeSet,
add-info                 [1] IMPLICIT AddInfo OPTIONAL
}

contents.html_ja: この文書は、鍵管理アプリケーションサービス要素（KMASE）が提供する SDNS 鍵管理属性ネゴシエーションサービスを定義します。属性ネゴシエーションサービスは、補足的なアクセス制御要件と、連携する SDNS コンポーネントが収容する特定のセキュリティプロトコル（すなわち SP2、SP3、SP4、SPN）の両方を支えるために、鍵管理アプリケーションプロセス（KMAP）が必要とする任意のセキュリティサービスを支える機能を提供します。属性ネゴシエーションサービスと、これらのサービスに関連する鍵プロトコルデータユニット（KPDU）の定義は、本来、鍵管理プロトコル（KMP）の一部です。したがってこの文書は、SDNS 鍵管理サービス定義およびプロトコル仕様（それぞれ SDN.902 と SDN.903）を直接補足するものです。
contents.html: This document defines the SDNS key management attribute negotiation service provided by the Key Management Application Service Element (KMASE). The attribute negotiation service provides facilities to support optional security services that are required by Key Management Application Processes (KMAPs) in support of both supplemental access control requirements, and the specific security protocols accommodated by the cooperating SDNS components (i.e., SP2, SP3, SP4, SPN). The attribute negotiation services and Key Protocol Data Unit (KPDU) definitions associated with these services are inherently part of the Key Management Protocol (KMP). This document, therefore, is a direct supplement to the SDNS Key Management Service Definition and Protocol Specifications (SDN.902 and SDN.903, respectively).

contents.html_ja: 双方が、KMASE の新規鍵要求（Nkrq）KPDU と新規鍵応答（Nkrs）KPDU の交換プロセスによって協調的な TEK を生成すると、開始側の KMASE が受信側の KMASE にセキュリティサービス要求（Ssrq）KPDU を送信し、受信側の KMASE がセキュリティサービス応答（Ssrs）KPDU で Ssrq に応答することによって、セキュリティサービスのオプションがネゴシエーションされます。Ssrq KPDU と Ssrs KPDU は、どちらも、直前の Nkrq と Nkrs の交換が成功した結果として生成された TEK を使って暗号化されます。したがって、Ssrs と Ssrq の KPDU の交換プロセスは、セキュリティサービス属性のネゴシエーションを提供するだけでなく、新たに生成された TEK についての相互の「生存確認」、すなわちピアの KMASE 同士の双方向認証としても機能します。
contents.html: Once a collaborative TEK has been generated by both parties, via the New Key Request (Nkrq) and New Key Response (Nkrs) KPDU exchange process of the KMASE, security service options are negotiated by the initiating KMASE by sending a Security Services Request (Ssrq) KPDU to the receiving KMASE, and the receiving KMASE responding to the Ssrq with a Security Services Response (Ssrs) KPDU. The Ssrq and Ssrs KPDUs are both encrypted using the TEK generated as a successful result of the preceding Nkrq and Nkrs exchange. Therefore, the Ssrs and Ssrq KPDU exchange process not only provides security service attribute negotiation, the exchange also serves as a mutual "liveness check" of the freshly generated TEK; i.e., bilateral authentication of the peer KMASEs.

contents.html_ja: 開始側の KMASE が送信する Ssrq KPDU には、proposed-options と呼ばれる、自らがサポートするサービスオプションのセットと、（任意で）add-info と呼ばれる、ドメイン固有の追加情報が含まれてもよいです。proposed-options 属性セットには、標準の、すなわちすべての KMASE が普遍的に理解するセキュリティサービスと属性のうち、開始側の KMASE が具体的にサポートするものが含まれます。すべての KMASE が理解するものの、開始側の KMASE がサポートしない標準のセキュリティサービスと属性は、開始側の KMASE の proposed-options セットに含められないだけです。任意の add-info には、標準のネゴシエーション属性に加えてネゴシエーションされてもよい、ドメイン固有の属性が含まれます。
contents.html: The Ssrq KPDU sent by the initiating KMASE may contain a set of service options that it supports, called proposed-options, as well as (optionally) additional information, that is domain specific, called add-info. The proposed-options Attribute Set contains the set of those security services and attributes that are standard - i.e., universally understood by all KMASE, and are those specifically supported by the initiating KMASE. Those standard security services and attributes understood by all KMASE, but not supported by the initiating KMASE, are simply not included in the initiating KMASE's proposed-options set. The optional add-info contains domain specific attributes that may be negotiated in addition to the standard negotiated attributes.

contents.html_ja: 一方、応答側の KMASE が開始側の KMASE に送信する Ssrs KPDU には、Ssrq KPDU の proposed-options の中から自らが選択したオプションのセット（selected-options と呼ばれます。Ssrq KPDU にこれらの属性が含まれていた場合の話であり、含まれていなくてもよい）と、任意で add-info データが含まれます。ただし、Ssrq KPDU で応答側の KMASE に送られた proposed-options または任意の add-info 属性が受け入れられない場合、応答側の KMASE は、Ssrq KPDU またはそのサービスオプションに誤りがあるか、応答側の KMASE の要件を満たしていないことを示す Estat KPDU で応答してもよいです。
contents.html: In turn, the Ssrs KPDU, sent to the initiating KMASE by the responding KMASE, contains a set of options that it has selected, from the Ssrq KPDU's proposed-options (given the Ssrq KPDU contained these attributes -i.e., it does not have to), called selected-options, and, optionally, add-info data. If, however, the proposed-options or optional add-info attributes sent to the responding KMASE in the Ssrq KPDU are unacceptable, then the responding KMASE may respond with an Estat KPDU, indicating that the Ssrq KPDU or its service options are in error or fail to meet the requirements of the responding KMASE.

contents.html_ja: KMASE の K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES サービスは、属性ネゴシエーションの活動を提供します。K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES サービスは、TEK との暗号上の互換性を検証し、TEK に関連する通信およびセキュリティ属性をネゴシエーションし、危殆化鍵リスト（Compromised Key List、CRL）の番号を交換します。さらに、K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES により、KMAP は以前の TEK の属性を新しい TEK に関連付けることができます。K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES のパラメーターを表 1 に示します。
contents.html: The KMASE K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES service provides the attribute negotiation activities. The K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES service verifies the cryptographic compatibility with the TEK, negotiates the communication and security attributes associated with the TEK, and exchanges Compromised Key List (CRL) numbers. Additionally, K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES allows a KMAP to associate the attributes of a previous TEK with a new TEK. The K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES parameters are illustrated in Table 1.

contents.html_ja: セキュリティオプションは、一方の KMASE（イニシエーター）が Ssrq KPDU をもう一方の KMASE（レスポンダー）に送信し、レスポンダーが Ssrs KPDU で返信することによってネゴシエーションされます。イニシエーターは、望ましいセキュリティオプションと代替のセキュリティオプションのセットを Ssrq KPDU で指定します。レスポンダーは、選択したセキュリティオプションのセットを Ssrs KPDU で指定します。
contents.html: Security options are negotiated by means of one KMASE (the initiator) transmitting a Ssrq KPDU to the other KMASE (the responder), which replies with a Ssrs KPDU. The initiator specifies a set of preferred and alternative security options in the Ssrq KPDU. The responder specifies the selected set of security options in the Ssrs KPDU.

contents.html_ja: イニシエーター KMASE は、K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES 要求プリミティブのパラメーターを使用して、レスポンダー KMASE 向けの Ssrq KPDU を作成します。Ssrq KPDU には、望ましいオプションと代替のオプションの一覧が含まれます。望ましいオプションのセットと代替のオプションのセットから省略されたオプションには、既定値が想定されます。Ssrq KPDU を形成した後、KMASE は icv を計算し、その後 KPDU を暗号化します。icv と暗号化の両方に使用される暗号鍵は、先に形成されたトラフィック鍵です。KMASE は、Ssrq KPDU をピアの KMASE に送信します。
contents.html: Using the parameters from the K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES request primitive, the initiator KMASE prepares a Ssrq KPDU for the responder KMASE. The Ssrq KPDU contains a list of preferred and alternative options. Default values are assumed for options which are omitted from the preferred and alternative sets. After forming the Ssrq KPDU, the KMASE computes an icv and then encrypts the KPDU. The cryptographic key used for both the icv and the encryption is the previously formed traffic key. The KMASE sends the Ssrq KPDU to the peer KMASE.

contents.html: On receipt of a Ssrq KPDU, the responder KMASE decrypts the preferred and alternative options and verifies the icv. If either of these operations fails, the KMASE sends a STAT KPDU to the peer KMASE indicating the cause of the failure. After decrypting and verifying the icv of the KPDU, the KMASE issues a K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES indication primitive to the responder. The KMASE now expects a K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES response primitive from the responder containing the selected options, and, optionally, add-info data.
contents.html_ja: Ssrq KPDU を受信すると、レスポンダー KMASE は、望ましいオプションと代替のオプションを復号し、icv を検証します。どちらかの操作が失敗した場合、KMASE は、失敗の原因を示す STAT KPDU をピアの KMASE に送信します。KPDU を復号し icv を検証した後、KMASE はレスポンダーに K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES 通知プリミティブを発行します。KMASE は、これ以降、選択されたオプションと、任意で add-info データを含む K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES 応答プリミティブが、レスポンダーから届くのを待ちます。

After forming the Ssrs KPDU, the KMASE computes an icv and then encrypts the KPDU. The cryptographic key used for both the icv and the encryption is the previously formed traffic key. The Ssrs KPDU is sent to the initiator KMASE.

The Secure Data Network System (SDNS) architecture and a set of associated specifications were developed through a multi-organizational project sponsored by the National Security Agency (NSA) They are presented here as a basis for standardization of

security services in the Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) architecture. The National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) intends to encourage widespread adoption of the resulting standards and the implementation of these security services into a wide spectrum of vendor products.

NIST is publishing the specifications that resulted from Phase I of the SDNS project for review and comment from potential government and commercial users of security products. The specifications are not complete or totally consistent, either internally or with a number of other security projects in the National and International Standards arena. Readers of these documents should recognize that these specifications are subject to modification for various reasons as they progress through the standards process. The sponsor and participants in the SDNS project are acknowledged for the work accomplished and their support in developing and releasing these specifications.

The SDNS project was initiated by NSA to investigate methods of implementing security in a distributed computer network. The results of this project include a set of specifications that include security services, protocols and mechanisms for protecting user data in networks that are based on the OSI computer network model. Productive security services that protect user data are specified and supportive security services, such as key management and access control, are also provided. No cryptographic algorithms are included in these specifications.

NIST is working with NSA and industry to identify and develop a framework of base standards for network security. In 1989, NIST established the OSI Security Laboratory where interested researchers from government and industry develop and demonstrate new ideas in network security. The major goals of NIST's network security activities are to:
Identify and develop security standards for open systems
Specify a key management system that supports these security standards
Encourage the development of interoperable equipment

NISTIR 90-4262 includes four documents dealing with key management which were developed by the National Security Agency (NSA) as output from the Secure Data Network System (SDNS) project. SDN. 601, Communication Protocol Requirements for Support of the SDNS Key Management Protocol, supplies a profile for the implementation of SDNS Key Management services in Open Systems. It is primarily concerned with providing guidance for implementation agreements on the variety of protocol stacks that are needed to satisfy the Key Management Application Process (KMAP) requirements in various communication specific environments. It also specifies the protocol support required at the transport, network, data link, and physical layers for varying communication environments; namely Packet Switched Networks (PSN) Local Area
Networks (LAN) and direct dial Public Switched Telephone Networks

SDN. 902, Definition of Services Provided by the Key Management Application Service Element (KMASE) defines in an abstract way the , key management services within the OSI Application Layer in terms of
a) the primitive actions and events of the service;
b) the parameter data associated with each primitive action

The standard only defines the services in terms of an abstract model. It implies neither a particular implementation of the services, nor does it imply a particular representation of the service primitives.

The protocol specified in SDN. 903, Specification of the Protocol for Services Provided by the Key Management Application Service Element, describes the KMASE services provided to the Key Management Application Process (KMAP) to support applications in a distributed open systems environment. Key management provides for the generation, distribution, and updating of traffic encryption keys. Some management capabilities for authentication and access control are provide by the KMAP.

SDN. 906, SDNS Traffic Key Attribute Negotiation, specifies the framework of the SDNS security attribute negotiation service. It supplements SDN. 902 and SDN. 903 where traffic key security service attributes negotiation is specified.
The four key management documents of NISTIR 90-4262 support the security protocols addressed in NISTIR 90-4250 and the access control documents covered in NISTIR 90-4259.
Comments and feedback are solicited by NIST.

This document specifies a profile for the implementation of SDNS Key Management services in Open Systems. It is primarily concerned with providing guidance for implementation agreements on the variety of protocol stacks that are needed to satisfy the Key Management Application Process (KMAP) requirement in various communication specific environments.
This profile specifies the protocol support services the

Application Control Service Elements (ACSE), the ISO Presentation layer kernel, and the ISO Session layer. It also specifies the protocol support required at the transport, network, data link, and physical layers for varying communication environments; namely, Packet Switched Networks (PSN), Local Area Networks (LAN), and direct dial Public Switched Telephone Networks (PSTN).
Use of ASEs and Lower Layer Services

The protocols referenced in the following paragraphs are required to provide the basic connection oriented message traffic, at ISO layers seven through five, for use in performing key management functions. At layer four and below, several difTerent options are available to support a variety of envisioned SDNS connection and connectionless oriented environments.
protocol stack alternatives are depicted in Figure 1. As illustrated in figure 1, the KMASE always requires the services of the ISO layer 7 ACSE, the ISO

layer 6 Presentation kernel, and the ISO Session Protocol, at layer 5. The Presentation and Session layer protocols shall be implemented in accordance with Government Open System Interconnection Profile ((jrOSIP) standards, which supplement ISO standards for SDNS components developed for U.S. Government use.

For Department of Defense (DoD) Transmission Control Protocol (TCP) and Internet Protocol (IP) implementations, the ISO Session layer must be mapped to the DoD Transport layer. The specifics of this mapping are beyond the scope of this document.

The Transport layer will use ISO TP class 0 when direct dial PSTN connections are required. For SDNS key management support, TP(0) will only be used in conjunction with the "public domain” X.PC specification. The Transport layer requires ISO TP class 4 when the ISO Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP) is employed for SDNS key management support. The DoD’s TCP must be used for the transport layer when the DoD Internet Protocol (IP) is employed at the connectionless network layer. The use of DoD’s TCP is dependent upon a standard mapping convention from the ISO Session layer, as stated above.
ISO Session Layer to DoD Transport Layer (TCP) "protocol bridge” is not a standard.
ISO Presentation, Session, and Transport Layers may be supplemented by GOSIP for U.S. Government components.
ISO Transport Layer classes I, 2, and 3 are not used for SDNS Key Management.

At the Network layer, the ISO CLNP standard is employed when ISO TP(4) is utilized at the Transport layer. CLNP may interface to X.25 layer 3, or to the Data Link layer for broadcast LANs (IEEE 802 standards). The DoD EP connectionless network protocol is used when DoD TCP is utilized at the Transport layer. IP may interconnect to an underlying X.25 layer 3, or to the data link layer for LANs using IEEE 802 standards.

At the Data Link and Physical layers, CCITT’s X.25 and/or DDN X.25, or IEEE 802 standards may be employed. For direct dial, the X.PC "public domain” protocol shall be used. X.PC is specified in publication number NPD-269, available, without charge, from McDonnell Douglas.

(Note that it is also viable for ISO TP(4) to use ISO CONS without a connectionless network layer. It is also viable, in some parts of the world, to have X.25 virtual circuit LANs. Both of these are prominent implementations and terminology used in Europe, primarily as a result of PTT controls. If or when SDNS devices are available for export to European countries, this is an important consideration for SDNS implementors.)

ACSE is specified in ISO 8650/2. All Specific Application Service Elements (SASE) -i.e., what the KMASE is in the ISO application layer, use ACSE to establish, release, and abort connections with peer SASE. All ACSE Protocol Data Unit (APDU) types and service primitives specified in the ISO standard are required for all SDNS key management applications.
Cooperating SDNS implementations shall support all mandatory parameters specified in the ACSE protocol standard. Unsupported parameter options shall not result in a protocol error.

Connection oriented Presentation protocols (PP) exist to ensure that the information content of APDUs and KPDUs are preserved during their transit between application entities. Functions performed by PP include negotiation of transfer syntaxes and transformation to/from transfer syntax. Services include connection establishment and release, context management, and information transfer. Cooperating SDNS devices shall use a single transfer syntax for KPDUs.

Connection oriented Session Protocol provides the means for the organized exchange of data between cooperating application entities. Services provided by the protocol include the establishment and release of connections and the exchange of data in an orderly manner.

Cooperating SDNS implementations shall support all SPDU types and primitives used by the session kernel, duplex, and expedited data functional units. All mandatory parameters shall be supported for each of the functional units. Details of the functional units and SPDU parameters are defined in ISO 8327. Unsupported
parameter options shall not result in a protocol error or discard.

Where DoD TCP is the underlying Transport layer protocol, there shall exist a mapping of the ISO Session Protocol and the DoD TCP. Such mapping shall be defined in an appropriate DoD standard. Until such a standard is available, implementors are discouraged from implementing this form of protocol stack.

Connection oriented Transport Protocol Class 4 provides reliable transparent transfer of data between cooperating KMAPs which operate over the connectionless-mode network service. Services provided by TP4 include the means to:
establish transport connections and negotiate Quality of Service (QOS) parameters;
transfer Transfer Service Data Units (TSDU) with or without concatenation and separation, segmenting and separating, and splitting and recombining;
transfer expedited TSDUs subject to separate flow control; and,

TP(4) shall be implemented when the underlying network protocol is the ISO Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP). Cooperating TP4 implementations shall support all Transport PDU (TPDU) types and primitives used by the Session service to transfer KMP data between cooperating SDNS devices. All mandatory parameters for TPDUs shall be implemented, as defined in ISO 8073 and DIS 8073/AD2,
Unsupported parameter options shall not result in a protocol error or discard.

Connection oriented Transport Protocol Class 0 provides transparent transfer of data between cooperating KMAPs operating over ISO connection oriented network service protocols. Services provided by TPO include the means to:

TP(0) is required to support all SDNS key management exchanges in the "dial-up” access mode. This access mode requires the underlying services of the X.PC "public domain” protocol. Details of TPO TPDUs and Session Protocol primitives are defined in ISO 8073. Cooperating TPO implementations shall support all TPDUs and Session Protocol primitives, and all mandatory parameters. Unsupported optional
parameters shall not result in a protocol error or discard.

TCP is required to support SDNS key management exchanges that are compelled to operate within internets that already exist with a significant number of IP routers. This kind of implementation is not encouraged, but may be necessary in some cases to keep the cost of deploying SDNS components to a minimum; for example, where IP routers are the only available routers on networks where SDNS devices are to be deployed. Consistent implementations of this type may not be feasible until ISO Session layer to DoD transport layer protocol mappings are standardized.
Details of TCP TPDUs and primitives are defined in Military Standard (MILSTD)
Cooperating TCP implementations shall support all TPDUs and Session
Protocol (mapped) primitives (To Be Determined) and all mandatory parameters.
Unsupported optional parameters shall not result in a protocol error or discard.

The ISO CLNP shall be used when the ISO TP Class 4 transport protocol is employed. Details of CLNP NPDUs and primitives are defined in ISO 8473. CLNP NPDU primitives and all mandatory parameters shall be implemented in accordance with ISO 8473. Unsupported optional parameters shall not result in a protocol error or

The DoD IP shall be used when the DoD TCP transport protocol is employed. Details of EP NPDUs and primitives are defined in MILSTD 1777. IP, including the Internet Control Message Protocol (ICMP), primitives and all mandatory parameters shall be implemented In accordance with MILSTD 1777. Unsupported optional parameters
shall not result in a protocol error or discard.

The X.25, layer 3, shall be used for SDNS key management exchanges that use either TCP/IP or TP(4)/(I)NLP for X.25 network connectivity. Details of X.5 PLP NPDUs and primitives are defined in ISO 8348. X.25 PLP NPDU primitives and all mandatory parameters shall be implemented in accordance with ISO 8348.
Unsupported optional parameters shall not result in protocol error or discard.
(Note: Where DDN and/or BLACKER X.25 layer 3 implementation are required, variances from ISO 8348 may be required.)
2.6. Data Link and Physical Layer Protocols
2.6.1. Direct Dial Public Switched Telephone Network Data Link and Physical Layers

The X.PC "public domain” protocol shall be used for all key management exchanges that are required over direct dial PSTNs. Details of the X.PC protocol are available from McDonnell Douglas, under the publication title NPD-269. For SDNS key management exchange support, the X.PC protocol shall operate in the packet mode only; i.e., not the character mode.

(Note: X.PC also has some network layer functionality, (i.e., addressing, packet assembly/disassembly, and multiple virtual circuit support - even through the underlying connection is strictly circuit switched [point-to-point].))
2.6.2. IEEE 802.x Data Link and Physical Layer Protocols

IEEE 802 protocol standards shall be employed for key management exchanges that are required over LANs. Details of 802.2, 802.3, 802.4, and 802.5 are available from the IEEE. It is envisioned that there may be some diversion from the specifics of IEEE 802.2 and 802.3 standards for various Ethernet (a trademark of Xerox Corporation) implementations.
2.6.3. CCITT X.25 Data Link and Physical Layer Protocols
Implementors that employ X.25 protocols shall do so in accordance with CCITT X.25 protocol specifications at layers 2 and 1.

This section defines the key management services as provided by the Key Management Application Service Element (KMASE). The services defined are of the category Specific Application Service Element (SASE), It provides facilities to support the key management activities required by and in support of cooperating Key Management Application Processes (KMAP) including the establishment of traffic encryption keys (TEK), the updating of TEKs, the distribution of Certificate Revocation Lists (CRL), and the interactive and staged rekey with the Key Management System (KMS).
This specification defines in an abstract way the key management services within the OSI Application Layer in terms of;
a) the primitive actions and events of the service;
b) the parameter data associated with each primitive action and event; and
c) the relationship between and the valid sequences of these actions and events.

This standard only defines the services in terms of an abstract model. It implies neither a particular implementation of the services, nor does it imply a particular representation of the service primitives. As this is a service definition, there are no conformance testing requirements.

This document uses definitions contained in the Reference Model for Open Systems Interconnection (ISO IS 7498/1) including the Security Architecture (ISO IS DIS 7498/2).
In addition the following definitions are used:
Credentials - information exchanged between SDNS components which authenticates each component and used to form a TEK between the components.
Certificate Revocation List - the list of key material identifiers which have been invalidated.
key material - information supplied by the KMS that contains a component's credentials and private information.
Initiator - the KMAP which initiates the establishment of an application association.
Rekey — the process by which new key material is obtained from the KMS either directly or via a rekey agent.
Rekey Agent — a SDNS component authorized to act as an intermediary between the KMS and other SDNS components for the delivery of key material.
Responder — the KMAP which responds to a request for establishment of the application association.
Signed - a method used to provide authentication of the originator of a message.
Universal-ID — identifies the universal to which a credential belongs.

This part of the specification uses the descriptive conventions in the OSI

Service Conventions in ISO/TR 8509. In Section 9, the definition of each service includes a table that lists the parameters of its primitives. For a given primitive, the presence of each parameter is described by one of the following values
In addition, the notation ( = ) indicates that a parameter value is semantically equal to the value to its left in the table.

This service definition uses the abstract model for a service defined in the OSI Service Conventions in ISO TR 8509. The model defines the interactions between two cooperating KMAPs. The KMAP consists of two parts: the information processing part, and the communication part, which is represented by the KMAE. When communication is required between two KMAPs, an application association is established between invocations of the processes’ KMAEs. The KMAE represents an
addressable set of communication capabilities which are defined by the the ACSE.

The KMASE is driven by service request and response primitives from the KMAP and by indication primitives from the presentation service provider. The KMASE, in turn, issues indication and confirm primitives to the KMAP, and issues request primitives to the ACSE and the presentation service provider.

The KMAP administers the Management Information Bases (K-MIB and the TEK-MIB) in the sense of updating data in the MIBs upon receipt of indications and confirms, and retrieving parameters from the MIBs when issuing requests and responses. The K-MIB is a security MIB used to store key material. The TEK-MIB is a security MIB used to store the TEK, KID, and attributes regarding the use of the TEK.
These services require information exchange with other SDNS KMAPs and with the KMS KMAP. The following services are provided:
a) Exchange TEK and security service information with other SDNS components.
c) Perform rekey operation with or with a rekey agent. Seed key conversion is a special case of the rekey operation.
d) Obtain the Certificate Revocation List (CRL).
e) Report cryptographic key usage errors and routing information.
This standard defines the following services for key management:
The K-EXCH-CRED service enables a KMAP to exchange credentials with a
for the purpose of mutual authentication and subsequent
The K-TRY-ME service enables a KMAP to inform a cooperating KMAP that it is authorized to provide security services for a specific network service access point.
The K-NO-KEY service enables a KMAP to inform a cooperating KMAP that traffic has been received protected under a key for which the receiver has no valid KID.

The K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES service verifies the cryptographic compatibility of a TEK, negotiates the communication and security attributes associated with the TEK, and exchanges CRL numbers. Additionally, K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES allows a KMAP to associate the attributes of a previous TEK with a new TEK.
The K-UPDATE-TEK service enables a KMAP to update a TEK without exchanging credentials.
The K-IREKEY service enables a KMAP or Rekey Agent KMAP to interactively obtain new key material from the KMS. Multiple sets of key material may be obtained by sequential use of this service.

The K-GET-CRL service enables a KMAP to obtain a CRL from a cooperating KMAP (e.g. the KMS KMAP). The new CRL is delivered only if the requestor has an older version of the CRL than the responder.

This document uses definitions contained in the Reference Model for Open Systems Interconnection (IS 7498/1) including the Security Architecture (IS 7498/2).
In addition the following definitions are used:
Credentials - information exchanged between SDNS component which authenticates the component and is used to form a traffic encryption key between the components.
Certificate Revocation List — the list of key material identifiers which have been invalidated.
key material — information supplied by the KMS that contains a component's credentials and private information.
Initiator — the KMAP which initiates the establishment of the application association.
Rekey — the process by which new key material is obtained from the KMS either directly or via a rekey agent.
Rekey Agent — a SDNS component authorized to act as an intermediary between the KMS and other SDNS components for the delivery of key material.
Responder — the KMAP which responds to a request for establishment of the application association.
Signed - a method used to provide authentication of the originator of a message.
Universal-ID — identifies the universal to which a credential belongs.

The KMAP administers the K-MIB and the TEK-MIB in the sense of updating data in the IB upon receipt of indications and confirms and retrieving parameters from the IB when issuing requests and responses. This procedure is used to exchange the credentials necessary to form a traffic encryption key (TEK) for communications between SDNS components.
This procedure uses the following KPDUs and parameters:
The credentials required to establish a TEK are exchanged by one KMASE (the initiator) transmitting a Nkrq KPDU to the other KMASE (the responder), which replies with a Nkrs KPDU.

The initiator KMASE uses the parameters from the K-EXCH-CRED request primitive to build a Nkrq KPDU. This KPDU contains the initiator's KID for the new TEK (init-kid), the universal-ID (univ-id), and the initiator's credentials (init-cred). This Nkrq I^DU is sent to the responder KMASE.

On receipt of an Nkrq, the responder KMASE issues a K-EXCH-CRED indication primitive to the KMAP. The responder KMASE now expects a K-EXCH-CRED response primitive from the KMAP containing the responder KID and the responder's credentials.

The responder KMASE uses the parameters from the K-EXCH-CRED response primitive to prepare a Nkrs KPDU, when the parameters indicate a successful exchange. This KPDU contains the initiator’s KID for the new TEK (init-kid), the responder’s KID for the new TEK (resp-kid), and the responder’s credentials (resp-cred). The Nkrs KPDU is sent to the initiator KMASE. If the K-EXCH-CRED
response primitive indicates a failure result, the responder ABORT request primitive to the ACSE.
When the initiator KMASE receives the Nkrs KPDU, it issues a K-EXCH-CRED
indicating the success of the exchange credentials

This procedure uses the following KPDUs and parameters:

The initiator KMASE uses the parameters from the K-TRY-ME request primitive to prepare a Tryme KPDU. This KPDU contains the end-system address served by the initiator KMASE (end-sys-addr). The initiator KMASE sends the Tryme KPDU to 7t.h3e. cooperating KMASE. The initiator KMASE does not expect any response.
When the responder KMASE receives a Tryme KPDU, the responder KMASE issues a K-TRY-ME indication primitive to the KMAP. The responder KMASE does not expect a K-TRY-ME response primitive.
The No Key procedure is a notification to a SDNS KMASE that traffic has been received which is protected under an invalid key.
This procedure uses the following KPDUs and parameters:

The initiator KMASE uses the parameters from the K-NO-KEY request primitive to prepare a Nokey KPDU. This document defines the SDNS key management attribute negotiation service provided by the Key Management Application Service Element (KMASE). The attribute negotiation service provides facilities to support optional security services that are required by Key Management Application Processes (KMAPs) in support of both supplemental access control requirements, and the specific security protocols accommodated by the cooperating SDNS components (i.e., SP2, SP3, SP4, SPN). The attribute negotiation services and Key Protocol Data Unit (KPDU) definitions associated with these services are inherently part of the Key Management Protocol (KMP). This document, therefore, is a direct supplement to the SDNS Key Management Service Definition and Protocol Specifications (SDN.902 and SDN.903, respectively).

This document applies to those SDNS key management applications which utilize the SDNS attribute negotiation process to apply specific security and communication attributes to a Traffic Encryption Key (TEK) immediately following TEK formation

The structure of the attribute negotiation parameters are specified using Abstract Syntax Notation One (ASN.l), as defined in ISO 8824. The ASN.l specified attributes defined in this document are intended to be "exported" to the KMASE ASN.l specifications, provided in SDN.903, where "AttributeSet" and "Add-Info" are called out as the specific placeholders. [Reference: SDN.903, pp 23]

The basic concept of the attribute negotiation portion of the KMASE is to establish the security and communication service attributes and conditions which are mutually acceptable to both the initiating and responding parties of the Traffic Encryption Key (TEK) generation processes of both KMASE. The KMASE TEK generation process is specified in SDN.902 and SDN.903.

Once a collaborative TEK has been generated by both parties, via the New Key Request (Nkrq) and New Key Response (Nkrs) KPDU exchange process of the KMASE, security service options are negotiated by the initiating KMASE by sending a Security Services Request (Ssrq) KPDU to the receiving KMASE, and the receiving KMASE responding to the Ssrq with a Security Services Response (Ssrs) KPDU. The Ssrq and Ssrs KPDUs are both encrypted using the TEK generated as a successful result of the preceding Nkrq and Nkrs exchange. Therefore, the Ssrs and Ssrq KPDU exchange process not only provides security service attribute negotiation, the exchange also serves as a mutual "liveness check" of the freshly generated TEK; i.e., bilateral authentication of the peer KMASEs.

The Ssrq KPDU sent by the initiating KMASE may contain a set of service options that it supports, called proposed-options, as well as (optionally) additional information, that is domain specific, called add-info. The proposed-options Attribute Set contains the set of those security services and attributes that are standard - i.e., universally understood by all KMASE, and are those specifically supported by the initiating KMASE. Those standard security services and attributes understood by all KMASE, but not supported by the initiating KMASE, are simply not included in the initiating KMASE's proposed-options set. The optional add-info contains domain specific attributes that may be negotiated in addition to the standard negotiated attributes.

The tree leaves contain a list of the remaining options. Illustrations, above, highlight which options are allowable for the security services and protocol modes selected. The remainder of this section describes each of the remaining negotiation options.

The confidentiality algorithm option is used for negotiating which symmetric algorithm(s) to use for the data confidentiality service of the security protocol and mode chosen. This algorithm is different than that used to form the TEK.

The integrity algorithm option is used for negotiating use of integrity algorithms, other than that used to form the TEK. This option includes the negotiation of the icv length. The icv length can be any of the following;

icv-len2 Integrity with a 2 byte icv length, icv-len4 Integrity with a 4 byte icv length, icv-len6 Integrity with a 6 byte icv length, icv-lenS Integrity with a 8 byte icv length, icv-lenlO Integrity with a 10 byte icv length, or icv-len12 Integrity with a 12 byte icv length.
The confidentiality and integrity algorithm option is used for negotiating use of
algorithms other than that used to form the for data security. This option includes the negotiation of the algorithm mode and the icv length, as defined above.

Security options are negotiated by means of one KMASE (the initiator) transmitting a Ssrq KPDU to the other KMASE (the responder), which replies with a Ssrs KPDU. The initiator specifies a set of preferred and alternative security options in the Ssrq KPDU. The responder specifies the selected set of security options in the Ssrs KPDU.

Using the parameters from the K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES request primitive, the initiator KMASE prepares a Ssrq KPDU for the responder KMASE. The Ssrq KPDU contains a list of preferred and alternative options. Default values are assumed for options which are omitted from the preferred and alternative sets. After forming the Ssrq KPDU, the KMASE computes an icv and then encrypts the KPDU. The cryptographic key used for
both the icv and the encryption is the previously formed traffic key. The
On receipt of a Ssrq KPDU, the responder KMASE decrypts the preferred and

alternative options and verifies the icv. If either of these operations fails, the sends a STAT KPDU to the peer KMASE indicating the cause of the failure. After decrypting and verifying the icv of the KPDU, the KMASE issues a K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES indication primitive to the responder. The KMASE now expects a K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES response primitive from the responder containing the selected options, and, optionally, add-info data.

Using the parameters from the K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES response primitive, the responder KMASE prepares a Ssrs KPDU. After forming the Ssrs KPDU, the KMASE computes an icv and then encrypts the KPDU. The cryptographic key used for both the icv and the encryption is the previously formed traffic key. The Ssrs
If the parameters of the K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES response primitive indicates a failure, the KMASE sends an Estat KPDU instead of a Ssrs KPDU.

On receipt of a Ssrs KPDU the initiator KMASE decrypts the KPDU and verifies the icv. The KMASE issues the K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES confirm primitive to the KMASE user application indicating the success or failure of the operation as well as the selected options, and, optionally, any add-info data.

If the initiator KMASE receives an Estat KPDU while awaiting the Ssrs KPDU, the KMASE issues a K-TEK-ATTRIBUTES confirm response to the KMASE user application indicating the failure of the option negotiation process.

The Secure Data Network System project, known as SDNS, implements computer to computer communications security for distributed applications. The internationally accepted Open Systems Interconnection (OSI) computer networking architecture provides the framework for SDNS. SDNS uses the layering principles of OSI to implement secure data transfers between computer nodes of local area and wide area networks. This publication includes four key management documents developed by the National Security Agency (NSA) as output from the SDNS project. SDN. 601 supplies a profile for the implementation of SDNS Key Management services in Open Systems. The definition of services provided by the Key Management Application Service Element (KMASE) is provided by SDN. 902. The protocol specified in SDN. 903 describes the KMASE services provided to the Key Management Application Process (KMAP) to support applications in a distributed open system environment. The framework of the SDNS security attribute negotiation service is described in SDN. 906.

original_blocks.html: The Transport layer will use ISO TP class 0 when direct dial PSTN connections are required. For SDNS key management support, TP(0) will only be used in conjunction with the "public domain” X.PC specification. The Transport layer requires ISO TP class 4 when the ISO Connectionless Network Protocol (CLNP) is employed for SDNS key management support. The DoD’s TCP must be used for the transport layer when the DoD Internet Protocol (IP) is employed at the connectionless network layer. The use of DoD’s TCP is dependent upon a standard mapping convention from the ISO Session layer, as stated above.

original_blocks.html: This service definition uses the abstract model for a service defined in the OSI Service Conventions in ISO TR 8509. The model defines the interactions between two cooperating KMAPs. The KMAP consists of two parts: the information processing part, and the communication part, which is represented by the KMAE. When communication is required between two KMAPs, an application association is established between invocations of the processes’ KMAEs. The KMAE represents an addressable set of communication capabilities which are defined by the KMASE and the ACSE.
